title: Which String Vibrations Become Which Generations on the Dwork Quintic: code, checks and engine record
description:
Code, independent checks and the record of the Anaxia engine for the paper Which String Vibrations Become Which Generations on the Dwork Quintic by Deep Bhattacharjee and Ushashi Bhattacharya.

The paper determines, for the heterotic string with the standard embedding on the one-parameter family of quintic threefolds, which vibration modes become which families of charged particles. The 101 families are labelled by 101 distinct characters of the symmetry group (Z/5)^3, and the 24 characters that do not occur are the classes of the permutations of (0,1,2,3,4). Every Yukawa coupling allowed by the symmetry is a power of the modulus, psi^r with r = 0, 1, 2, 3 on 566, 425, 280 and 160 unordered triples, and every other coupling vanishes. The invariant deformation pairs each family with exactly one partner, so that the mass matrix has determinant psi^70, full rank away from the Fermat point and rank 51 there, where the masses are given in closed form by the Gamma function. The Geometric Selection Conjecture is shown to be equivalent to the existence of one viable vacuum fixed by mirror symmetry, and no smooth quintic and no free quotient of one carries three families. On the three other one-parameter pencils of Fermat type, the sextic in P(1,1,1,1,2), the octic in P(1,1,1,1,4) and the dectic in P(1,1,1,2,5), the 103, 149 and 145 families carry only 96, 122 and 100 distinct characters of symmetry groups of order 108, 128 and 100; every coupling allowed by the symmetry is psi^r times a product of weights; the mass map of the invariant direction has rank 99, 125 and 109 at every member with psi nonzero, so 4, 24 and 36 families stay massless; and no member or free quotient carries three families. For the thirteen hypergeometric one-parameter Calabi-Yau complete intersections, every prime dividing the order of a group acting freely divides gcd(chi(L), chi(2L), chi(3L)), by the holomorphic Lefschetz formula; seven of the thirteen types, among them the sextic and the dectic, admit no free action at all, and no free quotient of any of them carries three families. The existence of a viable vacuum is open.

The archive holds 215 independent checks: a C program for the labels, the couplings allowed by the group and the mass map, a C++ expansion of the Hessian over its 120 permutations, Python checks of the socle, the Hessian, the intersection form of the Fermat quintic and the Gamma values, a Julia check of the Hodge norms, a Macaulay2 computation of the Jacobian ring at two rational values of the modulus with the socle functional on all 3876 monomials of degree fifteen, Python and Macaulay2 checks of the labels, characters, couplings, Jacobian rings and mass maps of the three weighted pencils, a Python check in exact arithmetic of the table of free quotients, and 14 Lean 4 theorems on the counts, the arithmetic of the Hessian and the numbers of the weighted pencils, each axiom-free or depending on propext only. code/run_checks.sh runs them all. code/bllm/ holds the failure, change and retry record of the five targets on the Anaxia engine (record made on release 3.1.0; current release 3.2.1, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23524945).
